title: Gentle weighted egress and ephemeral proxy quarantine for streamed sessions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Hosted API customers occasionally observe large RTOs and partial transcript loss when we shift traffic during regional capacity events. Existing hard cutovers and full proxy swaps cause TCP/HTTP/GRPC stream interruptions and client-side retries that overload neighbor regions. Goal: implement a controlled, weighted egress strategy combined with an ephemeral proxy quarantine layer that lets in-flight streaming sessions continue for a short grace period while new sessions are steered away, minimizing customer-visible interruption and avoiding cascade failures. This ticket covers design, implementation, and staged rollout of the mechanism across our gateway fleet.
acceptance_criteria: Canary: 1% of global traffic uses the weighted-egress controller and shows 0% increase in 99th-percentile streaming latency over baseline

Streaming continuity: active streams in source region maintain connection for a configurable grace period (default 60s) and then reconnect with a reconnect token to target region without losing conversation prefix in >= 95% of cases

Circuit breakers and load-shedding: when target region is overloaded, controller reduces weights with decay and triggers ephemeral proxy quarantine to reject new sessions with 503+Retry-After; overall P95 token latency must remain within SLOs
Observability: dashboards show per-region weight, active-ephemeral-proxies, per-session reconnect success rate, and estimates of token-cost impact
Safety: rollback toggle in console disables weighted-egress and drains ephemeral proxies within 30s (no manual host churn required)

comments: 2026-02-16 Asha Patel: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence. Key decision: prefer graceful weight decay over instantaneous cutover to preserve active stream continuity.

2026-02-19 Diego Morales: Prototype of weighted-e*gress controller completed. Uses sigmoid decay curve with backoff for overloaded target regions. Need runtime KV handshake spec before integrating streaming reconnects.

2026-02-22 Lena Fischer (SRE): Chaos run v1 showed 12% of streams failed to reconnect when target region had incompatible model variants; added compatibility check to controller to avoid steering to mismatched model versions.
2026-02-25 Security review: Determined reconnect tokens must be signed using customer-scoped KMS key; security_review_required=true and ticket to KMS team raised.

2026-02-28 Diego Morales: Implemented ephemeral proxy quarantine flags. Quarantined proxies accept only reconnect tokens and health-check traffic; new sessions receive 503+Retry-After with suggested retry jitter. PR #571 opened for review.
2026-03-01 PM review (Maya Chen): Aligning rollout with Dedicated customer announcements. Request to expose 'grace_period' per-customer via tenant config. Added as follow-up task.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full state replication to target region was rejected due to cost and write amplification; instead we rely on reconnect tokens + prefix KV cache warmup. We permit a short-lived ephemeral proxy to keep streaming sockets open to avoid client-side reconnect storms. Monitoring will pay special attention to redirected-rates and token reuse patterns to detect abuse.
